home.title: Backtesting framework mechanisms
home.intro: Inspect how portfolio decisions interact with actual execution. Each mechanism links to an interactive example and its implementation scope. Examples use synthetic data with explicit assumptions.
home.technical: Installation, API details and original reference
flow.question: How do cash and shares change?
flow.summary: Step through a buy and a sell, then reconcile cash and cumulative fees.
book.question: Why did only part of the order fill?
book.summary: Inspect the two fills, then compare actual shares with the later report.
cost.question: How much cash did this purchase spend?
cost.summary: Reconcile the cash debit, then calculate a separate missed opportunity.
impact.question: How does waiting change the second fill?
impact.summary: Compare recorded price offsets under different recovery assumptions.
lots.question: Which whole-share portfolios fit the budget?
lots.summary: Check 16 share pairs and see how minimum fees change feasibility.
paths.question: How do execution conditions change the account?
paths.summary: Compare four separate accounts under deterministic assumptions with no assigned probabilities.
selection.question: What gets selected from six trials with no signal?
selection.summary: Inspect every same-sample score before reading the selected result.
risk.question: How close was the risk forecast to the observed variation?
risk.summary: Compare predicted variance with observed residuals, then inspect missing results and account marks.
mechanism.portfolio.title: Portfolio optimization and nonconvex constraints
mechanism.portfolio.summary: Compare feasible portfolios when whole-share lots and minimum fees change the budget.
mechanism.portfolio.scope: Finite candidates can be checked exhaustively. Continuous impact planning has separate convex assumptions; general optimization belongs to the caller.
mechanism.feedback.title: Partial execution and subsequent decisions
mechanism.feedback.summary: Reconcile filled holdings, available cash and pending orders before the next allocation.
mechanism.feedback.scope: The example covers partial fills and delayed reports. Opportunity cost is covered in the cost lesson; network cancellation latency requires separate acceptance.
mechanism.cost.title: Transaction costs and opportunity shortfall
mechanism.cost.summary: Inspect fees and execution-price offsets in the account, then compare missed trades against an explicit counterfactual.
mechanism.cost.scope: Each execution owner books its cash fees. Opportunity shortfall requires a declared comparison and is not debited again as a cash fee.
mechanism.impact.title: Transient and permanent impact
mechanism.impact.summary: Change order size and waiting intervals to inspect modeled execution offsets and residual impact.
mechanism.impact.scope: Coefficients are assumptions. Permanent-impact sensitivity and rolling planning have distinct contracts; actual-fill calibration is unavailable.
mechanism.paths.title: Independent scenarios and market paths
mechanism.paths.summary: Repeat execution under supplied market and liquidity conditions, then compare accounts and subsequent actions.
mechanism.paths.scope: Every path has an independent account. Paths come from the caller; the illustration assigns no real-world probabilities.
mechanism.microstructure.title: Event replay and order-book microstructure
mechanism.microstructure.summary: Follow ordered events through matching, inspecting depth, partial fills and same-price priority.
mechanism.microstructure.scope: The separate order book supports FIFO replay. The current Nautilus product adapter is L1; L2 integration and real queue-position estimation need acceptance. This illustration covers only finite-depth execution.
framework.title: How the mechanisms connect
framework.note: Conceptual flow. Each backend retains its declared scope; connections do not imply one backend implements the combined capabilities.
framework.feedback: Actual fills and available state inform the next decision
advanced.title: Account reconciliation and further validation
advanced.intro: Use the account walkthrough to reconcile experiments. Selection bias and risk forecasts have separate diagnostic lessons.
comparison.title: Relationship to other frameworks
comparison.intro: Compare execution and planning separately. Upstream capabilities require adapter inputs, outputs and acceptance before use here. These links describe current upstream documentation, not acceptance of our pinned version.
comparison.nautilus.title: NautilusTrader
comparison.nautilus.summary: The main native execution foundation. Upstream supports depth books and latency models; our current fixed product adapter exposes L1 sessions.
comparison.hft.title: HftBacktest
comparison.hft.summary: A candidate independent comparator for queue position and latency. No production integration; historical replay has explicit own-impact limitations.
comparison.backtrader.title: Backtrader
comparison.backtrader.summary: Strategy backtesting with cost and slippage extensions. No integration planned; validate the existing execution foundation first.
